title: Compact Capacity Ledger: GPU Pool Health Snapshot and Burst Tuning Microflow
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design a compact, single-line 'capacity ledger' widget for the Redwood Console that surfaces GPU pool health, short-term autoscale intent, burst settings, and a one-click tuning microflow. Target use: operators and SREs who need a high-density health strip in list views and as a pinable quick-action in cluster detail pages.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger component renders as a compact horizontal strip at 44px height and contains: health shimmer, SLO compliance badge, current allocs, burst toggle, predicted cost delta and an affordance to open the full burst editor.
Tuning microflow allows change of burst window (minutes), burst headroom (%), and a cpus/gpu ratio preview with safe-guarded defaults and immediate preview of cost impact.
Interactions must be accessible (keyboard, screen reader labels) and meet AA contrast for badges.
Prototype flows (view-only, quick-tune, rollback) linked and validated in usability session with at least 3 internal operators.
Engineering signoff on feasibility for 3 variants: list-compact, detail-pin, and alert-expanded.
Design tokens and iconography align with Console theme; assets checked into figma and a minimal CSS spec provided.
Telemetry hooks enumerated for: tune_attempt, tune_commit, tune_revert, view_snapshot.
No breaking changes to existing Dedicated dashboards; toggle behind feature-flag for initial rollout.
design_notes: Motivation: operators are overwhelmed by wide dashboards. Need a dense 'at-a-glance' ledger that reduces time-to-action for burst tuning and reduces context-switching into the full capacity editor.
Trade-offs: showing predictive cost delta in-line improves decision speed but increases cognitive load; solution: use a muted hover-preview and a 1-click expand for the numeric breakdown.
Prototype variants: (A) minimal read-only strip with health + SLO + burst pill; (B) interactive microflow inline editing; (C) pinned detail with extended forecast sparkline.
Safety: changes initiated from microflow default to dry-run preview and require explicit confirm. Rollback button available within 10 minutes of commit via the ledger history affordance.
Performance: keep change payloads lightweight; microflow only sends delta parameters to backend (no full pool re-spec) and relies on server-side validation.
A11y: use aria-live region for commit success/failure and aria-describedby for cost preview. Keyboard focus order must follow: toggle -> burst field -> preview -> confirm/rollback.
Visual language: use condensed KPI typography; adopt a 3-color health scale (green/amber/red) with a neutral 'paused' state. Use micro-animations for burst activation to indicate transient state.
Estimations: front-end ~2 days to implement UI components + 1 day for telemetry hooks; backend ~3 days for validation endpoint and cost estimator (if not present).
